description: This source file 'chainlint.pl' is a Perl script designed to analyze shell script files for potential problems, specifically related to test definitions and their syntactical correctness. It contains modules for tokenizing and parsing shell scripts, identifying test constructs, and reporting issues such as broken command chains or unclosed heredocs. The script also supports command-line options, multi-threaded execution, and detailed error reporting.

classes.name: Lexer
classes.description: Tokenizer module that converts shell script source code into tokens, handling special shell syntax, comment, string literals, here-docs, and operators.

classes.name: ShellParser
classes.description: Recursive descent parser for POSIX shell scripts, capable of parsing commands, control structures, functions, and nested compound commands.

classes.name: TestParser
classes.description: Subclass of ShellParser with semantic analysis specific to test definitions within shell scripts, checking for common pitfalls and problems.

classes.name: ScriptParser
classes.description: Further subclass of ShellParser that identifies individual test definitions in scripts and applies TestParser to test bodies for issues.

methods.name: new
methods.description: Constructors for Lexer, ShellParser, TestParser, ScriptParser classes, initializing their state.

methods.name: parse_cmd
methods.description: Parses a shell command or construct into tokens, used recursively.

methods.name: parse
methods.description: High-level entry point for parsing an entire shell script source into tokens.

methods.name: check_test
methods.description: Analyzes a test definition for problems, using TestParser for detailed syntax checks.

methods.name: format_problem
methods.description: Generates human-readable descriptions of detected problems.

methods.name: unwrap
methods.description: Extracts raw content from tokenized test body for readability.
